text:
Sam Patel: Hey team, started getting 401 invalid_api_key on /v1/chat/completions this morning. No deploys or key rotations on our end, it just started failing.
Jordan Lee: Can you paste the curl you used (redact most of the key) and the Authorization header exactly as sent?
Sam Patel: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H \"Authorization: Api-Key \uFEFFsk_live_ABC123DEF...\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-4\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}]}'
```
Sam Patel: note: that \uFEFF is me trying to show an invisible char, not sure what it is.
Priya Nair: That looks like a UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF). If the key starts with BOM bytes (EF BB BF) the server sees non-matching value and rejects it as invalid.
Jordan Lee: Quick repro check: on your machine run `echo -n \"sk_live_...\" | xxd` and see if output starts with `ef bb bf`.
Sam Patel: ran it and got:
```
00000000: efbb bf73 6b5f 6c69 7665 5f41 4243 3132  ...sk_live_ABC12
00000010: 3344 4546 2e2e 2e
```
Sam Patel: so yep, there are EF BB BF bytes before the key.
Priya Nair: That usually happens when a secret file was created on Windows with a BOM or when pasted from some editors. When that file is mounted/used as-is the header contains three extra bytes.
Priya Nair: Quick fixes:
- Inspect: `kubectl get secret mysecret -o jsonpath='{.data.api_key}' | base64 --decode | xxd`
- Remove BOM in shell: `kubectl get secret mysecret -o jsonpath='{.data.api_key}' | base64 --decode | sed '1s/^\xEF\xBB\xBF//' | base64 | xargs -I{} kubectl patch secret mysecret -p "{\"data\":{\"api_key\":\"{}\"}}"`
- Or locally: `printf "$(cat keyfile)" | sed '1s/^\xEF\xBB\xBF//' > keyfile.clean` then update secret from file.
Jordan Lee: Another safe approach: open secret in editor that shows invisible characters or use `python -c "print(open('keyfile','rb').read())"` and check first bytes.
Sam Patel: We had exported the secret from a Windows machine and stored the key in a file that got base64'd into the k8s secret. Removing the BOM fixed it for us.
Sam Patel: Removed BOM from the secret and calls started succeeding again :white_check_mark:
Jordan Lee: Great — glad it was just a hidden-bytes issue. If you suspect the key copied someplace public, rotate anyway.
DevOps Bot: Secret mysecret updated by Sam Patel at 2026-03-17T14:12:50Z (automated message).
